source.title: Impaired sensitivity to Pavlovian stimulus-outcome learning after excitotoxic lesion of the ventrolateral neostriatum

confidence_rationale: Solid Dunnett-lab lesion study that adds a third dissociable striatal territory to the established DMS (goal-directed) / DLS (habit) pair: the ventrolateral striatum (VLS) is shown necessary for using a Pavlovian stimulus-outcome association to guide behaviour, while sparing both instrumental goal-directed action and habit. Taken with the DMS/DLS literature, it evidences a three-way functional parcellation of the striatum -- three territories with dissociable lesion signatures -- which is the parcellation the three-gate reading of Q-019 predicts over a single convergent gate. Confidence held at 0.6 because the striatal axis here (goal-directed / habit / Pavlovian-incentive) is not the same axis as Q-019's sensorium / thought / motor-commitment triad; it supports dissociability-of-territories in principle rather than the specific three loops.
failure_signatures: If the striatum implemented a single convergent selector, an excitotoxic lesion of any one subregion should produce a graded global deficit across instrumental and Pavlovian control; instead the VLS lesion selectively impairs Pavlovian-stimulus-guided responding while leaving instrumental goal-directed action and habit intact -- a selective, not global, signature.

If the three striatal territories were functionally redundant, VLS loss should be compensated by DMS/DLS; the persistence of the specific Pavlovian deficit indicates non-redundant, dissociable functions.

mapping.source_claim_statement: The ventrolateral neostriatum is a third functionally distinct striatal territory: its lesion selectively impairs the use of Pavlovian stimulus-outcome associations to guide behaviour, while leaving intact instrumental goal-directed action (a DMS function) and habitual responding (a DLS function) -- extending the DMS/DLS dissociation to a three-territory scheme.
mapping.ree_translation: Supports the three-gate over single-gate reading of Q-019: the striatum is not one convergent action selector but a set of anatomically distinct territories, each with a dissociable lesion signature on its own control axis. This is the parcellation principle three-gate requires -- distinct gating loci rather than one gate scoring several criteria.
mapping.mapping_caveat: The three territories here (DMS goal-directed / DLS habit / VLS Pavlovian-incentive) are NOT the same three loops Q-019 posits (sensorium-attention / thought-trajectory / motor-commitment). The paper evidences that striatal gating is functionally parcellated with dissociable lesions -- supporting three-gate-in-principle -- but does not map territory-for-territory onto the REE loops. Rodent lesion-behaviour dissociation to REE substrate transfer also applies.
mapping.source_context: Quinolinic-acid excitotoxic lesions of the ventrolateral neostriatum in rats; sensory-specific outcome devaluation for instrumental goal-directed action; Pavlovian approach with devaluation; test of habitual (devaluation-insensitive) responding.

confidence_components.notes: Good source quality (careful triple-condition lesion design, established lab), lower journal impact than the Nature/EJN entries. Mapping_fidelity moderate-low: strongly supports functional parcellation / dissociability of striatal territories but on a control-mode axis that differs from Q-019's loop axis. Transfer_risk moderate.
